items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: I think Jerry Wicksburg might have instituted that. You know, he may have, he could have been the person that instituted that at the time. The word may have, you know, around loosely. I'm not sure, but I think he did.

ctx.x: I think what he was saying is that, like yourself, many of the R&B artists who sang, or wrote, came from a church background. All of them started in church singing, and then took their talents, and their knowledge, and what they gave them to church, and then went to the studio and recorded. Yeah.

Well, I look at that twofold, because some of the people that really started in the church, I think Gospel music gave the individual a chance to reach out at what we call today, at the peak level of soul expression, as they used nowadays. So, and I think in the music loop, and you say this also, because many of the major recording companies used to come in, and this is the first thing you'd be singing something, and it's a, hey, stop. Like, you're not putting enough into it, you're just going to have enough for…

Okay. Why don't we, uh, in 1953, you did a record called Mother's Love. It's probably the first, the first record that went on the chart. Could you tell me something about that, how you don't want to record that?
